newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar closes off 8-1/2 year highs.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar closes off 8-1/2 year highs.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar touched fresh 8-1/2 year highs on Wednesday but had pulled back by the close.
The Kiwi was driven higher by buying out of Tokyo and was starting to look toppy by mid-afternoon.
Dealers said a wire service report that New Zealand First leader Winston Peters said easier monetary policy was part of coalition talks also served to push the kiwi off its highs.
It finished at US$0.7125/33 after touching a high of 0.7153, breaking the previous year high high of 0.7146.
On its Trade-Weighted Index it finished at 67.31 compared with its 67.66 high and against the 67.39 close on Tuesday.
Dealers said there was good support for the Kiwi at 0.7120 and if that held it was likely to push on to new highs.
"The buying interest seems to keep coming in as the euros and samurais keep coming in," said a Wellington bank chief dealer.
